normalized_hits.abstract: The mechanism distinguishing visual subitizing (small n ) from estimation (large n ) is unknown. We propose a theoretical mechanism based on the dynamical stability of an On-Centre Off-Surround (OCOS) recurrent neural network. A linear stability analysis of the model reveals that the spectrum of modal decay rates ( $$\lambda _k$$ λ k ) is parametrically controlled by numerosity ( n ) and inhibition ( $$\beta $$ β ). We derive that for small n , the system is highly stable, causing all noise-driven fluctuations to decay rapidly. As n increases, the network is tuned towards a critical boundary. This “critical slowing down” creates a dense spectrum of slow modes, which theoretically generates persistent, long-range temporal correlations (LRTCs). The model thus predicts that subitizing should be a dynamically memoryless (white noise) process, while estimation should exhibit persistent LRTCs (pink noise). To evaluate this prediction, we re-analyzed reaction time (RT) series from a continuous enumeration task. The empirical results aligned with our theoretical derivation: Subitizing RTs were effectively uncorrelated ( $$\alpha _{\text {DFA}}= 0.498 \pm 0.083$$ α DFA = 0.498 ± 0.083 ), matching the prediction for a stable system. In contrast, estimation RTs exhibited a mean exponent characteristic of dynamical persistence ( $$\alpha _{\text {DFA}}= 0.674 \pm 0.087$$ α DFA = 0.674 ± 0.087 ). Although high inter-subject variability limited the statistical significance of this contrast, the dynamical persistence in the estimation regime was behaviorally relevant: subjects with higher $$\alpha _{\text {DFA}}$$ α DFA exhibited a larger RT switch cost when moving from estimation to subitizing ( $$r \approx 0.41$$ r ≈ 0.41 ). We conclude that the subitizing-estimation divide may reflect a fundamental transition in the dynamical stability of the underlying neural system.

normalized_hits.abstract: AI-based song generation is rapidly advancing, using deep learning to create new and creative music. AI–generated music can create personalized soundtracks for different users and help artists come up with new musical ideas. In recent times, Large Language Models(LLMs) and transformer–based frameworks, music generated by these models sounds more natural, well–structured, and more flexible than before. This paper reviews all of the latest AI models used in music generation, including transformer models such as MusicGen and hybrid approaches that combine different neural network types . This study compares the datasets and tools used in research, including the MusicGen pre–training data set, the Million Piano-roll Dataset and other data sets built for specific styles or genres. Observations show that transformers are great for making well-structured music, while GANs are better at adding creativity and variation. LLMs are the most powerful and adaptable, but the field still needs better evaluation methods and more diverse data. To create AI music generation better, work should focus on common evaluation standards, global music data and smartly combined AI models.

normalized_hits.abstract: Monitoring the depth of anesthesia (DoA) is essential for ensuring patient safety during surgical procedures. Conventional approaches primarily rely on the Bispectral Index (BIS), derived from electroencephalogram (EEG) signals; however, BIS is sensitive to noise and inter-patient variability. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Transformer encoders for automated estimation of anesthesia depth from EEG data. The proposed model classifies anesthesia depth into four states: awake, light, surgical, and deep. CNN layers extract local temporal and spectral features from short EEG segments, while the Transformer encoder captures long-range temporal dependencies, enabling the integration of fine-grained and global patterns associated with anesthesia depth. The approach is evaluated using an open-source EEG and BIS dataset from Figshare. The performance of BIS predictions is evaluated by Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and the Pearson correlation coefficient. Experimental results show that the proposed CNN–Transformer model exceeds performance of CNN and CNN–LSTM baselines, providing a more robust and reliable estimation of DoA. This work highlights the potential of hybrid deep learning models for real-time, patient-specific anesthesia monitoring.

normalized_hits.abstract: Single-phase ground faults (SPGF) are the most common and frequent type of disturbance in medium voltage distribution networks especially under resonant or isolated grounding conditions for which high impedance and intermittent arc behavior are highly detrimental to the performance of traditional zero sequence and impedance grounding/G fault protection schemes. This paper proposes a non-intrusive intelligent identification framework, which integrates the clamp-on current sensing and voltage acquisition with the transformer-based large-scale artificial intelligence model for accurate SPGF detection. The methodology combines the building blocks of electrical fault modeling technique and time-frequency feature extraction learning coupled with global self-attention learning thus improves the transient signal discrimination un-der the complex operating conditions. Validation is done on an IEEE 11 kV test feeder considering variations of fault impedance between 10–1000 Ω, noise between 10–30 dB SNR and load fluctuation scenarios. The proposed approach is comparatively evaluated with five baseline models viz. Zero-sequence threshold, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Experimental results show 97.8% detection accuracy, F1-score of 0.97 and AUC of 0.99 as well as improvement of robustness and decreased false alarm rates. The framework provides a scalable, reliable and deployment-friendly intelligent protection for modern smart distribution networks.

normalized_hits.abstract: In response to the challenges faced by traditional manufacturing industries, such as low production efficiency, high costs associated with equipment maintenance and operation, and poor coordination during the production process, this paper proposes a digital transformation approach that integrates the Internet of Things (IoT) and intelligent monitoring algorithms. By constructing a four-layer technological architecture for “perception, transmission, analysis, and application,” the approach incorporates industrial sensors, 5G communication, and machine learning technologies to achieve data collection, intelligent diagnosis, and decision making optimization throughout the lifecycle of equipment manufacturing. The feasibility and effectiveness of this transformation path were validated through an example of the Dalian Shipyard. The results show that after implementing this approach, the accuracy of enterprise equipment fault alerts increased to 92%, production efficiency improved by 31%, and maintenance costs were reduced by 28%. This study provides a replicable technical solution and implementation paradigm for the digital transformation of the manufacturing industry, offering significant theoretical and practical value.

normalized_hits.abstract: Over the past few decades, there has been a substantial rise in date production in Tunisia. However, this growth in production has been marred by a notable increase in losses incurred during harvesting, storage, marketing, and technological processing. The significant quantities of by-products resulting from these losses remain largely unused by the population due to their poor quality. Biotechnological processing of lower-quality dates with a hard texture into derived products may give them a presentation, a structure and functionality. The aim of this work is to enhance the value of date fruit of inferior grades by using it in syrup production made according to different processing conditions. Four processes for date syrup preparation were used: conventional, by enzymatic extraction, microwave and intermittent processes (conventional—microwave) were investigated. The corresponding syrups were characterized and compared. The overall phenolic (TPC) and flavonoid (TFC) concentrations, along with their associated antioxidant capabilities were performed for each sample of the date syrup. Results showed effective outcomes of the used process for date syrup preparation on their functional properties. Date syrup prepared according to the combined process gave the highest phenolic and flavonoid contents (504.127 mg Gallic Acid Equivalent/100 g and 190.892 mg Catechin Equivalent/100 g of syrup respectively). The results of our study hold significant relevance for both researchers in the field and the fruit-processing industry. They offer opportunities to create novel food products with elevated antioxidant properties, aligning with the preferences of a contemporary consumer demographic.

normalized_hits.abstract: In the Mediterranean region, acorn fruits were generally used as animal feed for thousand years. At present, acorns are traditionally used for human consumption especially in bread and cake recipes. Thus, the objective of the present work was to highlight the interest of valorizing acorn fruits ( Quercus ilex ) from the north of Tunisia for the preparation of acorn flour as an alternative source of common wheat flour in order to produce cereal and gluten-free products. In this regard, the biochemical composition of the obtained acorn flour was studied. The phytochemical analysis in term of total contents of phenolics (TPC), tannins (TCT), flavonoids (TFC), and the HPLC profiles of the phenolic acids present in acorn flour extract were also determined as well as the composition of extracted acorn oil using gas chromatography. After that, the extracted acorn flour was mixed with semolina, wheat flour, and other gluten-free flours to determine the effect of its incorporation during the preparation of bread, pasta, muffin, cookies, and pizza. Results showed that acorn flour moisture was about 14.2%, whereas protein, ash, fat, and carbohydrates contents were 8.5%, 1.02%, 8.5%, and 66.78%, respectively. For TPC, TFC, and TCT, their contents in acorn flour were respectively, 20.55 mg GAE/g DW, 9.05 mg CE/g DW, and 1.21 mg GAE/g DW. In addition, we noted that the main phenolic acids were protocatechuic acid, ferulic acid, and gallic acid. Besides, oleic, linoleic, and palmitic were shown to be the main identified fatty acids in acorn fruits oil. Then, the efficiency of the substitution of wheat flour by the extracted acorn flour alone or in combination with other gluten-free flours was evaluated by pilot productions of cereal product such as: bread, pasta, muffin, cookies, and pizza. Results showed that the nutritional and rheological qualities of the formulated cereal products were improved with acceptable sensory properties.

normalized_hits.abstract: The international policies promoting renewable energy to reduce greenhouse gas emissions have resulted in agricultural land being converted to photovoltaic installations, leading to losses in food production. Agrivoltaics are systems that combine agricultural practices with solar energy production. Such systems involve installing photovoltaic (PV) panels on agricultural land or integrating them into structures such as greenhouses or shade structures. The primary goal of agrivoltaic systems is to maximize land use multifunctionality by promoting simultaneously solar energy for electricity production and carrying out agricultural activities. However, the agrivoltaic systems need careful planning and design to ensure that the shadow generated by PV panels doesn’t negatively impact crop production. Different crops have varying light requirements, and the orientation and height of the PV panels should be optimized accordingly. As the development of agrivoltaic farms is relatively new there is little knowledge of its crop production effects; therefore, further experimental applications are needed to assess the shadow and microclimate impacts generated by PV panel’s presence on the crops taking into account the heterogeneity of the agricultural sector. This study analyzed the effects of agricultural production under the shadow plots, mimicking the shadow impact of the PV panels, and in full sun plots as a control area. We chose chicory crop to highlight the differences in quantity and quality of crop production. Management cultivation practices, water availability, and soil composition were equally applied for all the analyzed plots to exclude environmental effects non-linked to the shadow. For each plant, weight, foliage dimension, and total secondary metabolites concentration were measured. The results showed a significantly high capacity of the shading system to increase edible chicory biomass production than the control plot with an increase in average weight biomass of 69%. Moreover, there was no relevant difference in the quality of crop production considering total secondary metabolites concentrations. We cannot exclude that in an agrivoltaic field these differences could be less significant, but it is possible to consider that a well-designed agrivoltaic system could be a good strategy to combine renewable energy strategies with food security increasing agricultural economic income.

raw_result.abstract: Monitoring the depth of anesthesia (DoA) is essential for ensuring patient safety during surgical procedures. Conventional approaches primarily rely on the Bispectral Index (BIS), derived from electroencephalogram (EEG) signals; however, BIS is sensitive to noise and inter-patient variability. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Transformer encoders for automated estimation of anesthesia depth from EEG data. The proposed model classifies anesthesia depth into four states: awake, light, surgical, and deep. CNN layers extract local temporal and spectral features from short EEG segments, while the Transformer encoder captures long-range temporal dependencies, enabling the integration of fine-grained and global patterns associated with anesthesia depth. The approach is evaluated using an open-source EEG and BIS dataset from Figshare. The performance of BIS predictions is evaluated by Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and the Pearson correlation coefficient. Experimental results show that the proposed CNN–Transformer model exceeds performance of CNN and CNN–LSTM baselines, providing a more robust and reliable estimation of DoA. This work highlights the potential of hybrid deep learning models for real-time, patient-specific anesthesia monitoring.

raw_result.abstract: Single-phase ground faults (SPGF) are the most common and frequent type of disturbance in medium voltage distribution networks especially under resonant or isolated grounding conditions for which high impedance and intermittent arc behavior are highly detrimental to the performance of traditional zero sequence and impedance grounding/G fault protection schemes. This paper proposes a non-intrusive intelligent identification framework, which integrates the clamp-on current sensing and voltage acquisition with the transformer-based large-scale artificial intelligence model for accurate SPGF detection. The methodology combines the building blocks of electrical fault modeling technique and time-frequency feature extraction learning coupled with global self-attention learning thus improves the transient signal discrimination un-der the complex operating conditions. Validation is done on an IEEE 11 kV test feeder considering variations of fault impedance between 10–1000 Ω, noise between 10–30 dB SNR and load fluctuation scenarios. The proposed approach is comparatively evaluated with five baseline models viz. Zero-sequence threshold, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Experimental results show 97.8% detection accuracy, F1-score of 0.97 and AUC of 0.99 as well as improvement of robustness and decreased false alarm rates. The framework provides a scalable, reliable and deployment-friendly intelligent protection for modern smart distribution networks.

raw_result.abstract: In response to the challenges faced by traditional manufacturing industries, such as low production efficiency, high costs associated with equipment maintenance and operation, and poor coordination during the production process, this paper proposes a digital transformation approach that integrates the Internet of Things (IoT) and intelligent monitoring algorithms. By constructing a four-layer technological architecture for “perception, transmission, analysis, and application,” the approach incorporates industrial sensors, 5G communication, and machine learning technologies to achieve data collection, intelligent diagnosis, and decision making optimization throughout the lifecycle of equipment manufacturing. The feasibility and effectiveness of this transformation path were validated through an example of the Dalian Shipyard. The results show that after implementing this approach, the accuracy of enterprise equipment fault alerts increased to 92%, production efficiency improved by 31%, and maintenance costs were reduced by 28%. This study provides a replicable technical solution and implementation paradigm for the digital transformation of the manufacturing industry, offering significant theoretical and practical value.

raw_result.abstract: Over the past few decades, there has been a substantial rise in date production in Tunisia. However, this growth in production has been marred by a notable increase in losses incurred during harvesting, storage, marketing, and technological processing. The significant quantities of by-products resulting from these losses remain largely unused by the population due to their poor quality. Biotechnological processing of lower-quality dates with a hard texture into derived products may give them a presentation, a structure and functionality. The aim of this work is to enhance the value of date fruit of inferior grades by using it in syrup production made according to different processing conditions. Four processes for date syrup preparation were used: conventional, by enzymatic extraction, microwave and intermittent processes (conventional—microwave) were investigated. The corresponding syrups were characterized and compared. The overall phenolic (TPC) and flavonoid (TFC) concentrations, along with their associated antioxidant capabilities were performed for each sample of the date syrup. Results showed effective outcomes of the used process for date syrup preparation on their functional properties. Date syrup prepared according to the combined process gave the highest phenolic and flavonoid contents (504.127 mg Gallic Acid Equivalent/100 g and 190.892 mg Catechin Equivalent/100 g of syrup respectively). The results of our study hold significant relevance for both researchers in the field and the fruit-processing industry. They offer opportunities to create novel food products with elevated antioxidant properties, aligning with the preferences of a contemporary consumer demographic.

raw_result.abstract: In the Mediterranean region, acorn fruits were generally used as animal feed for thousand years. At present, acorns are traditionally used for human consumption especially in bread and cake recipes. Thus, the objective of the present work was to highlight the interest of valorizing acorn fruits ( Quercus ilex ) from the north of Tunisia for the preparation of acorn flour as an alternative source of common wheat flour in order to produce cereal and gluten-free products. In this regard, the biochemical composition of the obtained acorn flour was studied. The phytochemical analysis in term of total contents of phenolics (TPC), tannins (TCT), flavonoids (TFC), and the HPLC profiles of the phenolic acids present in acorn flour extract were also determined as well as the composition of extracted acorn oil using gas chromatography. After that, the extracted acorn flour was mixed with semolina, wheat flour, and other gluten-free flours to determine the effect of its incorporation during the preparation of bread, pasta, muffin, cookies, and pizza. Results showed that acorn flour moisture was about 14.2%, whereas protein, ash, fat, and carbohydrates contents were 8.5%, 1.02%, 8.5%, and 66.78%, respectively. For TPC, TFC, and TCT, their contents in acorn flour were respectively, 20.55 mg GAE/g DW, 9.05 mg CE/g DW, and 1.21 mg GAE/g DW. In addition, we noted that the main phenolic acids were protocatechuic acid, ferulic acid, and gallic acid. Besides, oleic, linoleic, and palmitic were shown to be the main identified fatty acids in acorn fruits oil. Then, the efficiency of the substitution of wheat flour by the extracted acorn flour alone or in combination with other gluten-free flours was evaluated by pilot productions of cereal product such as: bread, pasta, muffin, cookies, and pizza. Results showed that the nutritional and rheological qualities of the formulated cereal products were improved with acceptable sensory properties.

raw_result.abstract: The international policies promoting renewable energy to reduce greenhouse gas emissions have resulted in agricultural land being converted to photovoltaic installations, leading to losses in food production. Agrivoltaics are systems that combine agricultural practices with solar energy production. Such systems involve installing photovoltaic (PV) panels on agricultural land or integrating them into structures such as greenhouses or shade structures. The primary goal of agrivoltaic systems is to maximize land use multifunctionality by promoting simultaneously solar energy for electricity production and carrying out agricultural activities. However, the agrivoltaic systems need careful planning and design to ensure that the shadow generated by PV panels doesn’t negatively impact crop production. Different crops have varying light requirements, and the orientation and height of the PV panels should be optimized accordingly. As the development of agrivoltaic farms is relatively new there is little knowledge of its crop production effects; therefore, further experimental applications are needed to assess the shadow and microclimate impacts generated by PV panel’s presence on the crops taking into account the heterogeneity of the agricultural sector. This study analyzed the effects of agricultural production under the shadow plots, mimicking the shadow impact of the PV panels, and in full sun plots as a control area. We chose chicory crop to highlight the differences in quantity and quality of crop production. Management cultivation practices, water availability, and soil composition were equally applied for all the analyzed plots to exclude environmental effects non-linked to the shadow. For each plant, weight, foliage dimension, and total secondary metabolites concentration were measured. The results showed a significantly high capacity of the shading system to increase edible chicory biomass production than the control plot with an increase in average weight biomass of 69%. Moreover, there was no relevant difference in the quality of crop production considering total secondary metabolites concentrations. We cannot exclude that in an agrivoltaic field these differences could be less significant, but it is possible to consider that a well-designed agrivoltaic system could be a good strategy to combine renewable energy strategies with food security increasing agricultural economic income.
